# Mobile build/publish workflows

`build-android.yml` / `build-ios.yml` — build `apps/native` with
`eas build --local`, uploading the `.apk`/`.aab`/`.ipa` as a GitHub Actions
artifact, optionally submitting straight to the Play Store internal track /
TestFlight.

`publish-android.yml` / `publish-ios.yml` — submit an artifact from a
previous build run (by `run_id`) without rebuilding.

## Why `eas build --local` instead of EAS's cloud build queue

This is a public repo, so GitHub Actions minutes are unlimited/free on
GitHub-hosted runners — macOS included. [EAS Build](https://docs.expo.dev/build/introduction/)'s
free tier is the opposite: capped at **15 Android + 15 iOS builds/month**,
low-priority queue. Building on the (free, unlimited) runner with
`eas build --local` instead of dispatching to EAS's (quota-limited) cloud
avoids that ceiling — the sensible default for an OSS project with plenty of
free CI compute already available.

`--local` still only talks to EAS's servers to fetch the managed signing
credentials (release keystore / iOS certificate + provisioning profile),
set up once via `eas credentials`. So this doesn't reintroduce manual
base64-keystore-in-a-secret handling — credentials stay centrally managed,
only the compute moves onto the runner. `apps/native` is an Expo *managed*
app: `android/`/`ios/` are generated by `expo prebuild` and gitignored, so
there's no committed `build.gradle`/`Info.plist` to hand-edit for version
bumps either way — `appVersionSource: remote` (`apps/native/eas.json`) lets
EAS own that.

Trade-off to know about: `eas build --local` artifacts are **not** registered
in EAS's own build list/dashboard (only cloud builds are), so the publish
workflows can't reference a build by EAS `--id`/`--latest`. They instead
download the GitHub Actions artifact from a specific `build-*.yml` run
(`run_id` input). If you'd rather have EAS's dashboard/build history and are
fine with the free-tier quota (or are on a paid plan), drop `--local` from
the `eas build` commands here and switch the publish workflows back to
`eas submit --id`/`--latest` — cloud builds also let iOS/Android compile
without needing `macos-latest`/preinstalled Android SDK on the runner at all.

## Beta testing: TestFlight (iOS) / internal track (Android)

Both are already the default path here, not a separate flow:

- **iOS** — every `eas submit --platform ios` upload goes through TestFlight
  processing first; there's no separate "beta" vs "production" submit call.
  Public App Store release is a distinct manual step afterward in App Store
  Connect, not something these workflows do. Always build with
  `profile: production` for anything headed to TestFlight — `preview`/
  `development` profiles are ad-hoc/dev-signed and Apple will reject them
  from TestFlight.
- **Android** — `eas.json`'s `submit.production.android.track` defaults to
  `"internal"`, so `build-android.yml`'s inline submit step lands on the
  Play Console internal testing track unless you pass a different `track`
  input. Use `publish-android.yml`'s `track` input to promote an already-
  submitted build to `alpha`/`beta`/`production` later without rebuilding.

## Runner requirements for `--local`

- Android: `ubuntu-latest` — GitHub's runner image ships a preinstalled
  Android SDK/NDK; the workflow adds a pinned JDK via `setup-java`.
- iOS: `macos-latest` — GitHub's runner image ships Xcode, CocoaPods, and
  fastlane, all required by `--local` (see
  [local build limitations](https://docs.expo.dev/build-reference/local-builds/#limitations):
  no `node`/`yarn`/`fastlane`/`cocoapods`/`ndk`/`image` overrides from
  `eas.json`, no caching — you own the toolchain versions on the runner
  image).

## Required secrets

| Secret | Used by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPO_TOKEN` | all four workflows | [Expo access token](https://docs.expo.dev/accounts/programmatic-access/) authenticating `eas-cli` non-interactively (also used by `--local` to fetch managed credentials) |
| `GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` | build-android (submit), publish-android | Play Console service account JSON key ([setup](https://docs.expo.dev/submit/android/#creating-a-google-service-account)) |
| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY` | build-ios (submit), publish-ios | App Store Connect API key (`.p8` contents) |
| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID` | build-ios (submit), publish-ios | Key ID for the above |
| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID` | build-ios (submit), publish-ios | Issuer ID for the above |

Use an App Store Connect **API key**, not an Apple ID + 2FA — the latter
can't run unattended in CI.

## First-time setup

```sh
cd apps/native
npx eas-cli login
npx eas-cli build:configure   # links this app to an EAS project, replaces the placeholder extra.eas.projectId in app.json
npx eas-cli credentials       # generate/upload the release keystore (Android) and signing certificate + provisioning profile (iOS)
```
